ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 18907, as amended) and its Enforcement Decree; Act on Regulation and Punishment of Criminal Proceeds Concealment (Act No. 17833, as amended); Financial Services Commission Regulations on Customer Due Diligence and Beneficial Owner Identification; Insurance Business Act for licensed captive reinsurer entities; Enforcement Decree of the Credit Information Use and Protection Act for identity verification obligations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Court Registry Office under the National Court Administration of the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Korean notary public certification, then Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea Apostille confirmation only for Apostille Convention jurisdictions. For non-member states, the certificate is authenticated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then consular legalized by the Korean embassy or consulate of the destination state. Apostille and consular legalization are never applied together.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Court Registry Office maintaining the corporate register of the Yuhan Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization and Hague Apostille by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Apostille Convention states. Consular legalization path for non-member states: Korean MOFA authentication followed by consular legalization at the Korean embassy or consulate of the destination country. No sequential apostille-plus-consular process.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney for Incorporation and Regulatory Submission
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Yuhan Hoesa, notarized by a Korean Licensed Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a Korean notary, then a Korean MOFA apostille for Apostille Convention jurisdictions. For non-Apostille jurisdictions, the notarized resolution is submitted to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for authentication and then to the competent Korean consular office for legalization. The two pathways are exclusive and never combined sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean Notary Public and the Court Registry Office with which the Yuhan Hoesa is registered
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille obtained from the Seoul Regional Chapter of the Korean Bar Association? No, the sole competent Korean authority is the Ministry of Foreign Affairs; in practice the local District Court may issue certified copies and the MOFA affixes the apostille. For non-member states, the certified articles undergo MOFA authentication and then consular legalization by the relevant foreign mission in Korea.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: A Korean commercial bank licensed by the Financial Services Commission, acting as the principal account-holding institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For recipients in an Apostille Convention member state, the letter is notarized at a Korean government-recognized notary and receives a MOFA apostille. For recipients in a non-member state, the letter must receive MOFA authentication and then consular legalization by the destination country's Korean embassy or consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and must never be chained.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, senior managers, captive beneficiary owners, and 10-percent-plus ultimate owners against the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit and Financial Supervisory Service disqualification databases, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions lists, EU consolidated financial sanctions, BIS Entity List, and domestic Korean sanctions. Enhanced due diligence requires lookback screening of politically exposed persons, their family members and close associates, adverse media, open-source risk flags, documented source of wealth and source of funds, and verified beneficial-ownership chain evidence. Any hit is escalated to the designated AML/CFT compliance officer and a 72-hour internal adjudication must be completed before commencement of the corporate formation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Commercial Registration Electronic System (eCourt Registry Portal, ecourt.scourt.go.kr) and Business Registration Portal of the Korean National Tax Service (HomeTax)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory trade name of a Yuhan Hoesa must be entered in the Korean Hangul script. A pure English or romanized name is not sufficient for court registration. The name must contain the Korean legal-form designator 유한회사 (Yuhan Hoesa) or the accepted abbreviation 유한, placed after the proprietary denomination. The four-tier naming composition covers: (1) the proprietary word-mark, (2) the concrete business purpose clause, (3) the registered head-office address, and (4) the capital contribution and shareholder liability form. English transliterations may be used in parallel only after the Hangul name is registered and must not be materially misleading as to the corporate form or licensed activity.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In the event of a name rejection, the applicant will receive a written notice stating the statutory reason. An administrative appeal must be filed with the competent District Court against the local Registry Office within fourteen (14) calendar days of the rejection notice using the 'Application against Refusal of Registration' procedure. The filing must specify the proposed Hangul name, the statutory ground relied on under Articles 27-29 of the Korean Commercial Act, and the absence of any prohibited token. The applicant may alternatively apply for ministerial approval from the Financial Services Commission if the rejected name contains a financial-industry term and evidence of a valid captive reinsurance license is produced. Legal counsel should prepare the appeal and any request for short-term name reservation extension, because the registry will only re-examine the name after a formal re-filing and, if necessary, a separate court hearing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office, shared commercial mailbox, or correspondence-only address is not permissible for a Yuhan Hoesa with a captive reinsurance business scope under ISIC 6512. The Financial Services Commission and the Financial Supervisory Service require licensed financial entities to maintain a fixed, independently identifiable physical place of business in the Republic of Korea, with a visible nameplate, physical records, telephone line, and at least one director or responsible employee present during business hours. The Korean National Tax Service will reject business registration if the address is merely a postal forwarding service, and Korean banks will refuse to open underwriting-reserve wire and SWIFT current accounts at a virtual-office address. If the purpose is only the holding of shares and passive management, a virtual office could be accepted for certain non-licensed holding companies; however, captive reinsurance underwriting triggers the statutory licensing requirement and therefore mandates a substantive physical office with employment and local operational substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced inspection: (1) correct street address and exterior nameplate; (2) physical file cabinets with board minutes and insurance policies; (3) principal staff present on site; (4) native Korean-language accounting and reinsurance records; (5) fixed assets and office equipment; (6) bank-account signature cards and SWIFT references; (7) compliance manual and AML/CFT internal policies; (8) valid business registration certificate on display. Quantified risk: for a newly licensed captive reinsurer, the Korean financial authorities conduct a planned on-site inspection within the first 18 months in roughly 85% of licensing cases. Unannounced physical inspections by the municipal registry or the National Tax Service occur with an approximately 40% likelihood during the first three years, and a full FSS on-site inspection may be triggered without notice by a material adverse finding in regulatory reporting. Announced and surprise joint inspections are common in the initial license years and must not be resisted.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Rules on Registration, etc. of Corporations, calculated on authorized capital and number of registered shareholders; standard court fee schedule of the Korean Supreme Court.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Supreme Court of Korea Commercial Registration Electronic System
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Nominal information-technology handling fee fixed by court administrative regulation; no ministerial or government service fee applies.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostille or consular legalization of the Articles of Association, Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Good Standing, Board Resolution and Power of Attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Korean Notary Public and Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille Office or destination-state consular office in Korea
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for Korean notarial tariffs and current MOFA authentication fee schedule, excluding court or legalization agency surcharges.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preliminary Financial Services Commission license application package for captive reinsurance SPV (ISIC 6512)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Financial Services Commission of the Republic of Korea
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Supervisory filing fee imposed by the Financial Services Commission Licensing Guideline and Financial Supervisory Service examination cost recovery rules; actual fee varies with asset scale and insurance product scope.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Senior cross-border corporate attorney formation retainer for Yuhan Hoesa constitutive documents and compliance audit
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Outside corporate law counsel in Seoul, Republic of Korea
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for cross-border financial-entity formation in Korea, charged as a fixed-stage retainer with an hourly component for enhanced due diligence; not a government tariff.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank reference letter and SWIFT/underwriting-reserve account onboarding documentation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank transaction and document-processing fee set by the bank's published tariff for corporate account documentation and authentication attestation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of Korean-language corporate instruments into English and apostille-ready plain-copy certification
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified Korean translation agency and approved notary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate per page for court-grade certified translation plus officer-level notarization fee under the Korean Certified Translation Association tariff.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of South Korea (Sangbeop, Act No. 1000 as amended), Articles 287-2 through 287-74 (Yuhan Hoesa limited liability company), especially Article 287-33 (incorporation registration), plus the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, Articles 5 and 6, for non-resident capital investment reporting.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Local District Court Registry Office (Registration Division under the Supreme Court Registration Affairs) with territorial jurisdiction over the Company's registered office; for a Seoul office, the Seoul Central District Court Registration Division.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Legal Entity (Beobin Seollip Deunggi Shinncheongseo) together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation (Jeonggwan) and attachments required by the Registration of Commercial Establishment Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Korean law imposes no minimum paid-up capital for a Yuhan Hoesa; however, the total contributed capital must be stated in the Articles of Incorporation and effectively paid in to a Korean bank account before the incorporation registration is filed. No blocked escrow account is statutorily required; the bank issues a certificate of capital deposit used by the registry as proof of contribution. Foreign currency remittance obligations follow foreign exchange reporting rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF YUHAN HOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY) 

RESOLVED, that the undersigned incorporator and initial director(s) of Yuhan Hoesa (Korea) Limited Liability Company (the "Company") hereby adopt and confirm the Company's Articles of Incorporation as notarized and presented to the competent Korean notary; that the initial contributed capital of the Company, being KRW 100,000,000 or such other aggregate amount as stated in the registered Articles of Incorporation, is hereby subscribed by the members in the proportions set forth in the subscription ledger; and that each subscription shall be paid in cash into the Company's domestic bank account no later than the date of filing the incorporation registration with the competent District Court Registry Office. 

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company shall be located at [address], in [City], Republic of Korea, and that such address is adopted as the Company's sole principal place of business, statutory seat, and address for service of process and regulatory correspondence; and that the Company shall lease such premises under contracts executed in the name of the Company. 

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Company shall open corporate operating, reserve, and underwriting trust accounts at [Bank Name], a commercial bank authorized to operate in the Republic of Korea; that the Representative Director and the Chief Financial Officer, acting jointly or severally as specifically instructed, are authorized to execute banking account forms, wire instructions, SWIFT transfer documents, treasury management arrangements, and FX settlement orders; and that any payment exceeding KRW 100,000,000 shall require two authorized signatures, unless expressly exempted by a subsequent board resolution. 

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the following statutory officers are hereby appointed to hold office until the first annual general meeting of members: (i) [Name] as Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer; (ii) [Name] as Chief Financial Officer; and (iii) [Name] as Compliance and Risk Management Officer responsible for regulatory filings, reinsurance licensing, AML/CFT measures, and internal governance. The Company's corporate seal and the signature specimens of all officers shall be registered with the local registry and notified to the Company's domestic bank. 

RESOLVED FINALLY, that the aforementioned officers be and are severally authorized to prepare, execute, notarize, lodge, and settle all documents, applications, certificates, tax registrations, foreign investment notifications, and reinsurance license submissions necessary to complete the incorporation and regulatory authorization of the Company, and to employ legal counsel, notaries, certified public accountants, and tax agents for that purpose.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Articles of Incorporation and Subscription of Membership Interests
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Korean Notary Public appointed under the Notary Public Act; for foreign investor documentation, also the relevant consulate or apostille authority.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founding members or their authorized legal counsel must prepare the Articles of Incorporation in the KoreanCommercial Legal drafting and ensure they comply with the Yuhan Hoesa provisions of the Commercial Act. The Articles must contain the corporate name including Yuhan Hoesa or Ltd. Co., the exact registered office address, the corporate purpose expressly limited to captive reinsurance SPV activities, the aggregate contributed capital, the number and nominal value of membership interests, the method of contribution, the treatment of interest transfer, the officers and their powers, the duration of the Company, and the accounting and audited reporting period. Each founding member must execute a separate subscription statement. If any founder is a non-resident entity, certified passport or corporate registration certificate, proof of beneficial ownership, and board authorization of the corporate founder must be obtained and notarized. The completed Korean-language articles and subscription documents must be notarized by the licensed notary, with English translations certified only for internal governance and foreign filing purposes.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation for Yuhan Hoesa
Subscription statement for each founding member
Passport copies or corporate registration certificates of all members
Board resolution or equivalent authorization of each corporate member
Certificate of beneficial ownership or identity verification
Power of attorney to local counsel or notary
English certified translation of the Articles of Incorporation
Lease intention letter or consent for registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses to notarize because the Articles are defective or incomplete, cure the defects by amending the Articles and resubmitting. If documents are rejected due to authenticity issues, request consular legalization or apostille and submit certified Korean translations. Supplement missing members' identification or authorization documents within five business days of the notary's inquiry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Capital Deposit Account and Verification of Paid-In Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A domestic commercial bank licensed by the Financial Services Commission and authorized as a foreign exchange bank, such as Kookmin, Woori, Shinhan, or Hana Bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before the incorporation registration can be accepted, the Company must open a temporary or pre-incorporation deposit account in the name of the prospective Yuhan Hoesa at a Korean commercial bank. Each subscribing member must remit in cash the full amount of their subscribed contribution by domestic wire or foreign exchange remittance. The bank will verify the receipt of the aggregate contributed capital and issue a certificate of capital deposit reflecting the name of each contributor and the total amount credited. This certificate is the definitive evidence of paid-in capital for the registry. For foreign investors, the capital remittance should be routed through a bank designated as a foreign exchange bank, and the bank will assist in generating the necessary foreign exchange report for the Ministry of Economy and Finance. The temporary account is not a blocked escrow account but is treated as a capital collection account for registration purposes.
required_dossiers: Application for opening the pre-incorporation capital deposit account
Executed and notarized Articles of Incorporation
Subscription statements of all members
Identification documents and powers of attorney
Foreign remittance instructions or SWIFT evidence for non-resident subscribers
Bank verification of foreign exchange receipt for KRW conversion
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries remittance origin or beneficial ownership, provide underlying bank statements and corporate ownership documents. If the remittance is blocked for AML reasons, submit transaction history and source-of-wealth evidence. If the account opening is delayed, use another licensed bank; however, the certificate must be a Korean bank certificate acceptable to the District Court Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for Incorporation Registration at the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Court Registry Office (Registration Division) with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office address of the Company.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Company, through its Representative Director or authorized attorney, shall file the application for incorporation registration with the relevant District Court Registry. The application must be signed and sealed in conformity with Korean notarial signature practices. The registry will examine whether the Articles are lawful, whether capital has been fully paid, whether the statutory officers have accepted their appointments, whether the registered office is real and accessible, and whether registration duty and local education surtax have been paid. The court staff may issue a supplementary order requesting corrections; the applicant must respond within the court-specified period. Once approved, the court enters the Company into the commercial registry and issues a certificate of incorporation registration, which is the official date of legal personality. The company may then obtain its corporate seal certificate from the local municipal office.
required_dossiers: Signed application for beobin seollip deunggi (formation registration)
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of capital deposit issued by the Korean bank
Subscription statements and contribution ledgers
Written acceptance agreements signed by all statutory officers
Identity documents and power of attorney to filing agent
Proof of payment of registration duty and local education surtax
Certificate of corporate seal consignment or seal imprint
Consent or lease agreement for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a supplementary order suspending the application, the applicant must cure the identified legal or documentary defect within the given cure period, usually two weeks. If the application is rejected, refile after correction without new substantive issues. If the registry refuses due to jurisdiction, transfer the application to the proper court. For unjustified refusal, an appeal can be filed under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure before the district court's appellate division.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Tax Registration and Business Registration with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through the District Tax Office having jurisdiction over the Company's registered office; local municipal government for minor licenses and local taxes.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 days after the issuance of the incorporation registration, the Company must complete corporate tax registration and obtain a business registration certificate (business taxpayer registration). The application is submitted electronically through Home Tax Service (HTS) or in person at the District Tax Office. The Company must provide the registry certificate, Articles of Incorporation, lease agreement, the Representative Director's identification, and bank account information. The NTS will issue a business registration number and determine whether the Company must register for VAT, withholding on wages, and corporate tax payment obligations using the electronic tax invoice system. The compliance office should ensure that the Company's stated purpose of captive reinsurance and the accounting records are sufficient to support tax status. The NTS may request proof of capital contribution, reconciliation of foreign exchange remittance, and the Company's anticipated profit and loss projections. After registration, the Company must file corporate tax returns and annual financial statements in accordance with the Corporate Tax Act.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation registration from the District Court
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Lease agreement or office ownership certificate
Business registration application form or electronic HTS data
Representative Director's identification and seal certificate
Bank account certificate and proof of capital paid-in
Foreign investment report or exemption documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS queries the business purpose or capital structure, submit a detailed business plan for the captive reinsurance SPV and proof of board approval. If filing is late or incomplete, pay the applicable late-filing penalties and file a corrected return. If the NTS imposes a registration suspension, use the administrative appeal process through the pre-assessment review or the Tax Tribunal while correcting the record.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Notification and Financial Regulatory Authorization for Captive Reinsurance Business
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: For foreign investment notification: Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) or the foreign exchange bank; for reinsurance licensing and supervisory compliance: Financial Services Commission (FSC) and Financial Supervisory Service (FSS).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If any founding member is a non-resident, the Company must file a foreign investment notice before or at the time of the capital remittance in accordance with the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The foreign investor should obtain a certificate of foreign investment registration from the bank or KOTRA. Independently, because the Company's intended scope is captive reinsurance under ISIC 6512, the Company must not commence underwriting activity until it has obtained a reinsurance business authorization from the FSS or a written exemption declaration from the FSC. The applicant must submit a fully implemented business plan, a capital adequacy and reserve plan, the intended captive ceding entities, the risk retention and retrocession structure, governance and AML/CFT arrangements, actuarial staffing plan, and financial forecasts. The FSC will consider whether the SPV is a pure captive for its parent corporate group and whether it satisfies solvency requirements under the Insurance Business Act and Insurance Supervision Regulations. A separate license or prior approval may be needed before accepting cross-border reinsurance risks from the parent and affiliated companies.
required_dossiers: Foreign investment report form (for non-resident members)
Certificate of capital deposit and foreign exchange remittance statement
Certificate of incorporation registration and tax registration
Notarized Articles of Incorporation and business plan
Captive reinsurance underwriting and retention plan
Credit ratings or group financial statements
AML/CFT compliance manual and governance charter
Actuarial report and loss reserve policy
Power of attorney to authorized counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the foreign investment report is incomplete, the bank or KOTRA will request supplementary information; remedy by filing corrected forms without restarting the grace period. If the FSS rejects or suspends the reinsurance license application, the Company may file a written explanation, amend the business plan, supply actuarial evidence, and reapply. If a final adverse determination is issued, judicial review may be sought in the Administrative Court; meanwhile, the Company must cease any unauthorized underwriting and may hold assets as a dormant SPV.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable for industrial or physical manufacturing licensing. For financial licensing: Financial Services Commission (FSC) and Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) under the Insurance Business Act.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable for physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing permits. Mandatory financial operating authorization: Reinsurance Business Authorization / Captive Reinsurance Approval under the Korean Insurance Business Act.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - no physical industrial facility; captive reinsurance is a financial service SPV with no construction, production, or discharge activity subject to the Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - no EIA registration, screening, or full EIA report required because the entity is an office-based licensed reinsurance undertaking.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no process wastewater, volatile organic compounds, or hazardous waste generated by captive reinsurance underwriting operations; standard office waste and electronic waste disposal under Wastes Control Act applies.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for an industrial Civil Defense fire permit or special structural load inspection. The entity's office premises must satisfy the Fire Services Act fire protection standards, Building Act occupancy safety, and Occupational Safety and Health Act workplace safety obligations applicable to financial offices, which are verified through ordinary building and fire inspection procedures.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, administered through the HomeTax electronic tax portal (hometax.go.kr); Korea Customs Service through the UNI-PASS electronic customs clearance system is the competent authority for export declarations. The local NTS district tax office with jurisdiction over the registered head office of KR_YUHANGHOESA handles the Business Registration Number and VAT registration account.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: STEP 1: The foreign non-resident investor completes the required foreign investment and foreign exchange declarations under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and files the captive reinsurance licensing application with the Financial Services Commission under the Insurance Business Act. STEP 2: Incorporate the Yuhan Hoesa (Korean limited liability company) in the commercial registry under the Korean Commercial Act. STEP 3: Before the commencement of business, submit the Business Registration Application to the competent NTS district tax office either through HomeTax or physically at the tax office. Attach the certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, board resolution, identity documents and power of attorney for the statutory representative and the local tax representative, evidence of paid-in capital sourced from the foreign non-resident shareholders, and the captive reinsurance license or preliminary license confirmation. STEP 4: The NTS verifies the commercial registry filing and license conditions and issues the 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN), which simultaneously constitutes the corporate Tax Identification Number (TIN) and the Value-Added Tax (VAT) registration number. STEP 5: Register the entity in HomeTax as an electronic tax invoice issuer, activate the HomeTax API or EDI submission credentials for e-invoice reporting, and file the VAT registration notification together with the regular corporate tax registration notification. STEP 6: If the foreign non-resident entity itself has no Korean business place, it does not require a domestic corporate BRN; its Korean resident subsidiary, Yuhan Hoesa, is the domestic taxpayer, while the foreign parent appoints a domestic tax representative for any withholding or administrative notices. The Yuhan Hoesa is a resident domestic corporation for all Korean tax purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the Yuhan Hoesa is a resident Korean domestic corporation subject to entity-level corporate income tax on worldwide income under the Corporate Tax Act and is not treated as a pass-through entity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korea does not provide a check-the-box or pass-through election for a Yuhan Hoesa. It is per se a taxable corporation. No hybrid mismatch or transparency election is available for this captive reinsurance SPV, and it cannot elect the simplified VAT regime applicable only to small individual businesses.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW 0 / no monetary threshold. A domestic corporation is compulsorily required to register for VAT before business commencement under Article 8 of the Value-Added Tax Act regardless of expected turnover. The captive reinsurance SPV must remain VAT-registered and file periodic VAT returns, reporting zero-rated and exempt supplies with corresponding restrictions on input VAT recovery for exempt financial and insurance services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT invoices in Korea must be issued and transmitted as Electronic Tax Invoices (ETIs) through the NTS HomeTax portal or a certified e-tax invoice service provider. ETI data must be transmitted to the NTS by the end of the day following the date of issuance, creating a real-time self-declared clearance and audit trail. There is no government fiscal stamp or pre-clearance authorization before invoice issuance; anti-fraud controls are achieved through real-time reporting, sequential invoice numbers, NTS certification of issuers, matching of purchaser submissions, and automatic exception analysis of missing or inconsistent ETIs. Taxpayers integrate accounting systems with the HomeTax OpenAPI or Internet-EDI channels for automatic invoice transmission. Failure to issue or transmit an ETI triggers automatic statutory additional tax, and deliberate omission is treated as a tax evasion indicator. For cross-border reinsurance services, the Korean yuhan hoesa must ensure that any domestic reverse-charge obligation for imported exempt or taxable services is correctly self-assessed, while retained evidence of zero-rating is kept contemporaneously.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 21 of the Value-Added Tax Act, exported goods and exported services supplied to non-residents are eligible for a 0% VAT rate if the transaction is substantiated by the statutory export documentation and foreign exchange repatriation evidence. For the captive reinsurance SPV, premiums received from a foreign ceding insurance group company can qualify as zero-rated exported services when the reinsurance contract is with a non-resident, the risk is located outside Korea, the premium is paid in a convertible foreign currency from an overseas account, and the service is economically rendered from Korea. If the zero-rating criteria are not met, the reinsurance service is ordinarily an exempt financial/insurance service under Article 26 of the Value-Added Tax Act, making the SPV unable to recover related input VAT. For qualifying offshore digital services, the same foreign-currency payment and non-resident recipient conditions apply, plus contemporaneous evidence that the digital service is not effectively used or consumed in Korea.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Export Declaration Confirmation (export bill of entry filed through UNI-PASS), including the HS commodity description and declared value in Korean won or foreign currency
Commercial invoice and packing list issued by KR_YUHANGHOESA to the non-resident buyer

Original Bill of Lading or, for air cargo, Air Waybill evidencing removal of goods from Korea; for captive reinsurance service exports, the executed reinsurance contract, placement slip, and board underwriting minutes evidence the offshore supply

Bank-issued Inward Foreign Exchange Remittance Certificate (FIRC-equivalent foreign exchange settlement receipt issued by an authorized Korean foreign exchange bank) proving that the premium or export price was wired from the non-resident counterparty in convertible foreign currency within the statutory export settlement period
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS may reopen an export zero-rating claim within the extended statutory reassessment period, which can reach 10 years for fraudulent or untruthful returns under the Framework Act on National Taxes. If the customs declaration, FX wiring, or reinsurance contract is not substantiated, the supply is recharacterized as taxable at the standard 10% VAT rate, with assessment of VAT, statutory additional tax for unfaithful returns or non-issuance of electronic tax invoices, and daily delayed-payment interest on the unpaid amount. False invoices, sham wiring, circular foreign-currency flows, or artificial offshore contractual structures are referred for criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, subjecting the statutory representative, directors, and materially contributing tax advisers to penalties including imprisonment and fines. For captive reinsurance, the NTS also scrutinizes economic substance, premium pricing against arm's-length standards, capital reserve adequacy, and compliance with the Insurance Business Act, and any clawback is retrospective from the date the original zero-rated supply was claimed.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) in conjunction with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and the Foreign Exchange Information System (EMTRAC) administration
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Korean won (KRW) operates under a partially convertible foreign exchange regime. Current account transactions, including reinsurance premium receipts for services rendered, are largely liberalized but remain subject to declaration and electronic filing through EMTRAC. Capital account transactions, including equity injections, foreign currency debt, and certain hedging products, require a preemptive declaration with a foreign exchange bank unless an explicit exception applies. The BOK and the MOEF maintain strict monitoring over cross-border funds flows to detect sudden reversal or speculative activity. For profit remittance, a captive reinsurer must first complete annual financial audits, settle all corporate and withholding taxes, and obtain a tax clearance certificate from the National Tax Service before receiving approval to remit dividends. Surrender requirements are operational, not conversion-like: exporters and service receivers must bring proceeds within a statutory deadline and may maintain the proceeds in foreign currency accounts without mandatory conversion. However, every receipt must be reported to EMTRAC, and conversion transactions must be executed through authorized foreign exchange banks at market rates. The convertibility is therefore full for operational settlements but contains procedural frictions and verification stages for capital flows, which must be baked into the treasury timeline.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export and service proceeds, including premium income under a captive reinsurance SPV, must be collected within one year from the date of the relevant trade declaration, extendable up to an additional six months upon MOEF approval. There is no mandatory conversion ratio to KRW; the entity may hold or utilise the foreign currency in a designated foreign currency account. All receipts must be individually reported to EMTRAC within one business day of collection.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Underwritten Capital Deposit) / KRW Operational Settlement Account
Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW & USD multi-currency)
Trade Settlement and Liquidity Reserve Account
Reinsurance Premium Collection and Claims Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital electronic money institutions (EMIs) cannot serve as the primary banking layer for a Korean-domiciled captive reinsurer. The Electronic Financial Transactions Act requires any entity holding customer funds or issuing multi-currency accounts to hold a Korean banking or electronic financial business license. Foreign EMIs such as Revolut or Wise Business do not hold such license and cannot maintain local settlement rails into EMTRAC, nor can they execute BOK/USD FX deliveries. Their utility is limited to payment card initiation and does not satisfy the statutory repatriation and tax reporting requirements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory for the statutory director (de facto board representative) when opening corporate banking accounts in Korea. Remote consular proxy opening is not permitted for local bank account application. However, for foreign signatories, a notarized Power of Attorney and apostilled certificate of incorporation may allow a designated officer in Korea to perform the branch appearance; video verification is accepted only as a supplementary step after the on-site identification. The bank's compliance committee may require a face-to-face interview with the Ultimate Beneficial Owner and CFO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Disproportionate related-party reinsurance exposure to a single foreign parent group without third-party risk distribution.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Actuarial certification from an accredited reinsurance intermediary showing arm's length premium pricing, loss ratios, and independent reserve valuation; group-wide reinsurance programs and elephant slip; evidence of risk distribution through outward retrocession with licensed third-party reinsurers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity and high-risk residency in a restricted or non-cooperative jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified chart of ownership and full UBO disclosure; notarized passport and proof of residence; source of wealth declaration supported by audited group financial statements; negative news and sanctions screening from LexisNexis or Dow Jones; an external legal opinion confirming the chain of title.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Numerous zero-value or negligible equity transactions in capital escrow account consistent with shell-company cash-flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized board resolution specifying the subscription amount, bank reference letter from the originating remitter showing the commercial purpose; certified copy of the Korean Business Registration Certificate; funds confirmation and SWIFT MT103 with its purpose code matching the licensee's capital verification form.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistency between expected premium volume and low operational substance (no employees, no local office).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Strategic onboarding evidence: lease agreement or office-sharing agreement in a licensed business center, actuarial staffing arrangement via a third-party management company, quarterly board meeting minutes, comprehensive 5-year business plan, proof of regulatory license application to the Financial Services Commission (FSC) for captive reinsurance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All equity injections must be routed via SWIFT MT103 to the designated Capital Deposit Escrow Account under the Korean bank's Foreign Currency Trading Code 201 (capital payment receipt). The remitter shall complete the EMTRAC report within one business day using Purpose Code 601 (Investment in Korean branch/subsidiary). The Korean bank will issue a Certificate of Foreign Exchange Receipt ('Foreign Exchange Bank Certificate') and the receiving company must file a capital verification report with the Korean customs authority or a licensed tax agent within 15 days after the deposit.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For reinsurance premium payments to foreign retrocessionaires, use SWIFT MT103 with purpose codes 603 (payment for services) and maintain full lodgement of underlying contract and loss reserve calculation. For claim settlements exceeding USD 10,000 or equivalent, Documentary Collection (D/C) and Commercial Letters of Credit (L/C) can be used; most treasury operations will prefer MT103 for speed. All outputs must be reported to EMTRAC within one business day.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore KRW/USD deliverable forward contracts (with AUD/MIT license of the dealing bank) solely for hedging underlying real exposure
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) may be considered through global interbank market but prohibited for domestic settlements; a subsidiary/direct offshore may use NDF
Interest-rate and cross-currency swaps available only for hedging of long-term non-trade liabilities under FSS pre-approval

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Final Return and related schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year entity, no later than March 31 of the following year; for a non-calendar fiscal year, within three months of the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-file surcharge of 20% of the unreported corporation tax; late-payment surcharge of 0.022% per day for up to three years; persistent delinquency triggers enforced collection, business registration revocation and director disqualification.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Income Tax Surcharge on Corporation Tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Si/Gun/Gu local government through the National Tax Service joint e-filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same statutory filing window as corporation tax, March 31 for calendar year-end entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Surcharge of 10% of the underdeclared amount plus daily overdue interest of 0.022% per day; default triggers local tax seizure and compulsory property sale.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Return for First Six Months
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: July 25 immediately following the January-to-June taxable half-year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing surcharge of 10% of unpaid VAT; late-payment surcharge of 0.075% per day; repeated violation may lead to criminal referral and business license revocation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Return for Second Six Months
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 25 immediately following the July-to-December taxable half-year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing surcharge of 10% of unpaid VAT; late-payment surcharge of 0.075% per day; repeated violation may lead to criminal referral and business license revocation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Independent Auditor's Annual Report on Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Members or shareholders; Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) for licensed captive reinsurers; annexed to NTS corporate tax return where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar year-end, report must be finalised and delivered within 90 days of December 31; FSS filing for licensed entities is due no later than March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to obtain a mandated audit is unlawful; administrative fines up to KRW 20 million may be imposed, the audit deficiency is recorded in the external audit information system, and the responsible representative is subject to sanctions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation and AML/CFT Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) under the Financial Services Commission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation by March 31 for calendar year-end; any transfer of units or change of beneficial ownership must be reported within 30 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to KRW 30 million and imprisonment up to one year for willful non-compliance; dividend and voting rights may be suspended until compliance is achieved.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Captive Reinsurance Regulatory Maintenance Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year-end, or within 90 days of any alternate fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-submission may trigger license suspension or revocation under the Insurance Business Act, administrative fines up to KRW 50 million, and temporary suspension of underwriting authority.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Korean Act on External Audit of Companies and the Insurance Business Act, a Yuhan Hoesa captive reinsurance SPV is statutorily required to undergo an independent certified public accountant audit if it meets any of these conditions: (i) total assets at the future-end are KRW 5 billion (approx. USD 3.8 million) or more; (ii) annual revenue consisting of gross premiums and investment income is KRW 10 billion (approx. USD 7.6 million) or more; (iii) it employs 300 or more regular full-time personnel; or (iv) it holds any insurance license, in which case a certified audit is mandatory regardless of size. If the SPV is consolidated by a parent applying K-IFRS, a consolidated audit is required without regard to the SPV individual thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) is mandatory for licensed captive reinsurers, public-interest entities and consolidated subsidiaries of K-IFRS parent groups; smaller non-licensed Yuhan Hoesa entities below audit thresholds may apply K-GAAP (Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Standards) or the Korean SME Accounting Standards. Statutory financial statements must be prepared in Korean Won and in the Korean language.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SPV must maintain a physical or electronic register of members and beneficial owners at its registered office. The annual UBO confirmation must be filed with KoFIU no later than March 31 following a calendar year-end; any share transfer, capital increase, redemption, or change in 10% or greater ownership must be reported within 30 days of the transaction being registered in the statutory books. Failure to update the register within the 30-day window exposes the company to administrative fines and restriction of shareholder voting and dividend rights.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% top corporate income tax bracket; with 10% local surtax, aggregate effective top rate 26.4%. Lower taxable-income brackets: 9% (for taxable income up to KRW 200 million) and 19% (for taxable income over KRW 200 million up to KRW 20 billion).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No captive-reinsurance-specific incentive. General R&D credits up to 30% of qualifying R&D spending under the Special Tax Treatment Control Act, and 5-year CIT exemption plus 2-year 50% reduction for qualifying high-tech foreign investment in free economic zones under the same Act. No patent box regime for reinsurance IP.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Standard Return (Filing Form No. 5) filed via the National Tax Service HomeTax e-filing portal (hometax.go.kr), with Schedule 76 'International Transactions Report' and the 'Application for Withholding Tax Reduction under Tax Treaty' where applicable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing must be made within 3 months after fiscal year-end (e.g., 31 March for a 31 December year-end). An interim prepayment return for the first half of the fiscal year is due within 3 months of the end of that half-year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 1a (Corporate Status and Non-Resident Ownership Declaration)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identifies the entity as a domestic Korean corporation and records the percentage of shares held by non-resident persons, list of foreign shareholder tax residencies, and their Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) numbers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an SPV 100% owned by a foreign parent, state 'domestic corporation'; list the parent's jurisdiction and TRC. If non-resident ownership exceeds 50%, attach a shareholding registry certified by the securities transfer agent. Incomplete disclosure can void treaty claims and triggers a 5% assessment under Article 76 of the Corporate Income Tax Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of net underwriting income, plus investment and incidental income, after deducting claims, reserves, commission, and management expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Capture gross reinsurance premium ceded from the foreign group; benchmark pricing using OECD methodologies (CUP, TNMM, etc.). Disclose any intra-group premium greater than arm's-length differential exceeding 3% (or 5% for financial transactions) in the transfer-pricing schedule; failure to do so invites a TP adjustment and a 10% surcharge on additional tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after deduction of carried-forward prior losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use NOL carryforward of 15 years but obey the 80% annual restriction for large companies. Non-resident investors cannot claim the Korean SPV's losses in their own tax returns; the Korean SPV's NOL is available only to the SPV itself and may be lost on change of more than 50% ownership unless statutory continuity is preserved.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit for income taxes paid to foreign jurisdictions on foreign-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the captive earns foreign-source investment income (e.g., interest on offshore reinsurance trust), attach foreign tax receipt and TRC. Credit is limited to the proportion of Korean CIT corresponding to foreign-source income / total income. No credit applies to distribution taxes paid by the parent; dividends from the SPV are not entitled to indirect credit as the SPV is a domestic entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory report of all cross-border transactions with foreign related parties - premium, claims, loss reserve funding, management fees, interest, royalties - and the transfer pricing method applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The form is mandatory if aggregate intercompany transactions exceed KRW 5 billion. State the pricing method, financial indicators, and components. Omission of a related party or transaction gives rise to a 10% additional penalty on the omitted transaction value and may invite criminal investigation under the Punishment Tax Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 15 (Paying Agent's Withholding Summary for Non-Residents)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declares the amount of withholding tax remitted on payments to non-residents, including outbound dividends, interest, royalties, and service fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For each payment, if treaty relief is sought, attach the 'Application for Withholding Tax Exemption/Reduction under Tax Treaty' and the beneficial owner's TRC. If the SPV fails to withhold because of an invalid treaty claim, the SPV is primarily liable for the uncollected tax (22%) plus late-interest of 0.022% per day.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or non-filing: 20% surcharge on the underpaid tax (40% if fraudulent) under Article 47-4 of the Framework Act on National Taxes; fixed penalty of KRW 200,000 when no tax is due. Late payment: daily interest at 0.022% of unpaid tax (approximately 8% annually) plus additional monthly surcharges. Criminal exposure for wilful evasion: imprisonment up to 3 years and fine up to 3 times the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate (20% national dividend WHT + 2% local surtax) when a Korean corporation distributes dividends to non-residents; reduced by DTA to 0-15% (e.g., 10% for direct shareholdings of at least 10% under the US-Korea treaty; 0-5% under certain treaties, subject to domestic law).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply the DTA, the non-resident shareholder must: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by its taxing authority within the same calendar year, naming the relevant tax article and evidencing legal residence; (2) submit to the Korean SPV, before each dividend payment, a completed 'Application for Withholding Reduction/Exemption under Tax Treaty' (available on HomeTax) executed by the shareholder or its authorized agent; (3) supply a beneficial ownership statement (including evidence that the shareholder is the true owner and bears the economic risk, has no contractual obligation to pass dividends to third parties, and is not an accommodation party); (4) retain supporting governance documents (board resolution authorizing dividend, capital ownership registry, updated TRC). The Korean SPV must withhold at the treaty rate based on these documents; if the documents are insufficient, it must withhold 22% and the shareholder may file a refund claim with the National Tax Service within 5 years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory: 22% (20% WHT + 2% local surtax) for both cross-border royalties and interest. DTA rates: interest typically 10%-15% (most treaties); royalties typically 5%-10% (reduced to 0% for royalties on software or copyright under some treaties); all reliefs conditioned on beneficial ownership and the principal purpose test (OECD MLI Article 7).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 5,000,000,000 for filing the International Transaction Report; Master File and Local File are required when aggregate foreign-related-party transactions exceed KRW 10,000,000,000 in a fiscal year, unless the SPV qualifies as a small business (documentation excused).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea has no statutory Economic Substance Regulation akin to UAE ESR, but under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs, the National Tax Service will apply the 'real business purpose and substance over form' doctrine in audits. A captive reinsurance SPV must prove its own premises, full-time and qualified personnel (actuary, risk manager, legal counsel), board meetings physically held in Korea, actual management of underwriting and investment decisions, and assumption of material risk. Failure to do so may result in disregarding the SPV for CIT purposes, reallocating income to its foreign parent, denying DTA benefits, and treating undistributed profits as deemed dividends for CFC purposes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion via Sham Reinsurance Transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Korean captive reinsurance SPV that executes non-arm's-length reinsurance arrangements (e.g., 99% ceding commission, retrocession to a shell tax-haven affiliate, or inflated loss reserves) without any real risk transfer or Korean economic substance, to shift the group's underwriting profits out of the Korean taxable base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 3 of the Punishment Tax Act, tax fraud is punishable with imprisonment up to 3 years, plus a fine up to 3 times the tax evaded; additionally, the corporate tax underreporting surcharge is 40% of the underpaid tax under Article 47-4 of the Framework Act on National Taxes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorized or negligently failed to prevent the sham arrangements are jointly and severally liable for the additional tax, interest, and penalties as transferors under Article 39 of the National Tax Collection Act. A criminal conviction includes imprisonment (up to 3 years), confiscation of proceeds, asset seizure, travel ban (blacklist), and disqualification from future directorship.
